div.head: Chapter 15
div.p: From what has been said, the second part of the order of divine and natural law stands proved; namely, that the Spaniards did not observe that their first entry should be slow and gradual and unhurried, giving those peoples to understand that they came for their benefit and welfare to win their goodwill; but rather, like lightning bolts from heaven, impetuously, violently, and suddenly, burning everything they touched, they fell upon them and did what has been recounted.

They appear likewise to have violated the third part of the said natural and divine order, by making an entry and first landing and disembarkation from the ships onto the land that was injurious and harmful to those peoples, since they entered without the license of the kings and lords and inhabitants of each province or land; causing such great alarm and scandal in some places that already had news of their deeds, fearing to suffer the harms and devastations they had inflicted on their neighbors, resisting their entry most justly. Which resistance was a most just natural defense, and beyond defense was a just war to punish them as enemy invaders and aggressors against foreign kingdoms and lordships, as was said in the first principle; and belonging to the fourth category, they had and have natural jurisdiction against us, and just and full authority.

That they also profaned the fourth part, which was to live as Christians so that the unbelievers might be moved by their good example and come to desire to receive our holy faith: who among all who live today in the world and its compass can be ignorant of this? Who could recount the detestable acts in every kind of ugliness and wickedness that our own — wretched men closest to eternal damnation — apart from the most cruel abominations and various impieties committed in the wars, have perpetrated in their conduct and manner of life, to the dishonor and blasphemy of the name of Christ and of all the Christian religion? How many robberies, thefts, rapines, acts of force and violence, and acts of enslavement, making slaves of free people, taking children from their fathers, daughters from their mothers, and so abandoning both to orphanhood against all natural law, usurpations of foreign lands and lordships, of private persons and of kings and commonwealths? How many adulteries, acts of violation, abductions of maidens, both single and married? And what they already hold as a most common and canonized thing, celebrated as a great virtue: to keep with them not one alone to abuse as they will, but three or four, and some of them many more. And so that nothing should be lacking to crown their unbridled life in the gravity of sins against God, there was one who made it his trade to buy idols from the Indians in one province to sell in another where he expected to sell them more dearly, after the idols had been abandoned and burned through the preaching of the friars; and the Indians complained, saying that the friars had deceived them by making them abandon their gods, which they knew to be better than those that Christian sold them. And finally in this trade he gave his soul to the devil. And that this was so became clear, because he died without confession, with several loads of idols under his bed, which certain Franciscan friars subsequently found there.

This is the life and example that those who carry from here the name of Christians have had and today have, and give to those unbelievers; and thus they esteem all who profess the Christian faith and religion to be the same, and that their God and their law, and their king likewise, have so ordered and commanded it. This was written by a bishop of Santa Marta of the order of Saint Peter, in the year forty-one, to the Emperor and to Doctor Bernal, who was then of the Council of the Indies. And today I hold in my possession one of these letters. Where he says the following: "There would be no Indian who was not a Christian and vassal of His Majesty, were it not for the vexations and hardships and torments the Spaniards inflict upon them. For which reason nothing is more odious or hateful to them than the name of Christian; and so they call them in their language devils. And without any doubt they have every reason for it, because the works they see them do are not those of Christians, nor even of men who have the use of reason, but of demons. From which it follows that, seeing this evil conduct so universal, both in the heads and in the members, they think that Christians hold this as their law and that their God and their king command it of them; and to labor to persuade them otherwise is to try to cast lances into the sea, and to give them occasion to laugh and mock and make scorn of Jesus Christ and of his law, etc." These are his formal words.

By this fourth part and violation of the divine and natural order, we may well be certain that no one who is a rational man, even if he be not learned, will deny that the first entry and indeed the whole course of the Spaniards in the Indies was and has been violent, most cruel, abominable, and tyrannical, and that of cruel enemies, and such that no wicked people could have made it worse.

That they broke and violated the fifth part; namely, that they should give notice of the final cause of their going, which was preaching, etc.: we will not take long to prove this, since their entry was nothing other than impetuously, plundering, burning, laying waste, ravaging and destroying and robbing those peoples, and bathing the towns and countryside in human blood — against all the gentleness, sweetness and mildness, modesty, grace and charitable love, and the long span of time required to declare and commend it to them. It is quite true that the final cause which moved them from these kingdoms to sail to those parts, they declared to them at great length and without delay; namely, that they should give them gold and silver, not the honor of God nor the salvation of souls. Which they made plain by the exquisite torments never before seen or heard of that they inflicted upon them to demand gold — having put into their hands everything they had — and suspecting they still had more, they gave them more torments, and with them killed them without any mercy. This was their entire ultimate end: this drew them out of Spain and led them there; this has governed and commanded and ruled them always; and for this they have defamed the Son of God and offended the whole most holy Trinity, and set the name of Christians in hatred and abomination; for this they have laid waste to those immense peoples and depopulated those lands of such breadth and length; for this they live always in a state of eternal damnation; and that for this it is impossible to be saved without the most grave penitence and full satisfaction for so many irreparable wrongs as they have caused: no Christian, unless he be a great beast and more faithless than a Christian, can doubt it.

The sixth part was that the Catholic faith should be preached distinctly, explicitly, freely, and at length, according to the form that Christ established. This preaching of the faith the Spaniards have favored and assisted in such a way that — with the truth of God I say this, understanding what I am saying — God has not had in the world greater enemies nor more effective impediters or obstructors of its growth and spread, in their efforts to obstruct it for their own interests, to obtain gold and acquire riches. They have differed from all the persecutors of the faith, gentiles or pagans, only in not having killed with their own hands the preachers who have preached it; but every obstruction and every persecution that can be devised, short of killing them, to rob them of all authority, they have done and sought, raising the most false accusations against them and swearing to God as a threat that if they did not leave the towns held in their encomiendas they would stab them to death. And so as not to escape being murderers of friars, at times they have been the cause of Indians killing some religious men, on account of the scandals they had given. And the wickedness of some went so far that they made the Indians of a certain province understand that the friars ate human flesh, and that they should not give them their children to be taught, because they would eat them when they least expected it. And there was a tyrant who ordered the Indians to beat a friar to death with clubs, and so they did, and so they left him dead. What they allege is that after the friars preach to them and make them Christians, they become too clever and cannot be made to serve, or the tributes they are ordered to give are impeded. And they say this because the Indians complain to the friars, and the friars advise the governors of the grievances and oppressions with which they torment them ceaselessly. And of such adversaries Saint Paul had those who impeded his preaching of the Gospel and the conversion of souls: "Forbidding us to speak to the Gentiles that they might be saved, to fill up their sins always; for the wrath of God has come upon them to the end." 1 Thessalonians 2.

In three ways the Spaniards impede and destroy the preaching of the faith and the salvation of souls in the Indies. The first, by killing and destroying those most infinite peoples before they hear a word of Christ, sending them to hell without faith and without sacraments. The second, by contradicting the Christian faith and doctrine through the many works, abominable examples, and wicked lives they lead and live. The third, directly, by forbidding the religious to enter the Indian towns to preach to the Indians, and stripping them of all authority and credit as much as they can.

I well believe that it stands proved that the Spaniards broke and violated the natural and divine order in this sixth part, and consequently that they have been tyrants, both in their entry and in their subsequent conduct together.

By everything we have brought as proof of the six parts of the order of natural and divine law, the seventh and final part appears proved; namely, that no contract, pact, or agreement was concluded between the party of our kings and lords of Castile and León and the kings and lords and peoples of that world or of any part of it, as natural and divine law necessarily required. For their entire intent and end was no other than to enter those kingdoms and lands and subjugate and lord it over them, and to obtain the riches and treasures that were in them; and the means they employed to achieve this their beloved and desired end were to kill and destroy, tear apart, and wreak devastation by diverse and novel forms of cruelty upon those nations, the natural lords and owners of those lands, as if all the Indies were pastures full of livestock, as they were full of peoples, and they had to fill their ships with dried meat to bring home; and it is certain they have made no more account of them than that. And so it appears how the Spaniards broke and violated the order of natural and divine law in all the parts it contains, and consequently the first part of the seventh principle; namely, that the first entry or foothold with which they entered the Indies and each part or place of them was tyrannical and most cruel, and worse than any barbarous nation would have done, or even cruel beasts: this appears manifest.
